VIDEO TILE (Lantern 1.24.43) -- REVIEW 4: THE NEWEST AND MENDED PARTS, USED AS A PERSON USES THEM
=================================================================================================
Reviewer: a separate agent that did not write the tile and did not copy reviews 1 and 2 (their reports were read
only to learn how the page is driven). Date: 2026-11-27.
Build tested: site/index.html of branch lantern-1.24.43 at commit dbd0ecf (md5 777536b3efd4f68c1330daf57315bc37),
in Playwright's Chromium (headless), 1400 x 900 unless said, also 390 x 844 and 1366 x 768. Line numbers below are of
src/lantern.inner.html at that commit. Nothing outside this folder was changed.

Files here
  run.py      self-contained. Makes its own media with ffmpeg in a temporary folder (removed at the end), serves
              ../../../site/index.html (or the build named as its first argument) and plays every scenario in headless
              Chromium by mouse and keyboard: menus clicked, tools picked by their letters (V B N R Y U), clips clicked
              and dragged on the Timeline canvas (with Shift and Alt held where a person would), the scroll bar and
              \ and - to bring frames into view, values typed into Effect Controls and the dialogs, stopwatches clicked,
              files chosen in the browser's file box, items dragged (HTML drag) from the Project panel and from the
              Source Monitor's Drag handle. Results are read from the app's state AND from what it shows or writes: the
              Program Monitor's canvas, frames drawn by Lantern.video.render.frame, the mix from Lantern.video.mix.range,
              the meters' canvases, and every exported file decoded by ffprobe and ffmpeg. One line per check, "PASS
              ..." or "FAIL ...  [what was seen]", then "<n> checks, <m> failed". Sections can be run alone:
                python3 run.py [build.html] [trims edits trans fx fx2 target undo keys exportsec project views more]
              A check's text names only the scenario and what is expected (never a value Lantern produced); "(Premiere)"
              marks a check whose expectation is Premiere Pro's behaviour rather than the tile's own Help.
  REPORT.txt  this file.

The media (made by run.py): tick.mp4 (320x240, 30 fps, 180 frames, H.264 with B-frames + AAC: its frame number in
binary in a row of boxes at the bottom; a white band at the top on frames 30-31, 90-91, 150-151 and a 2 kHz beep on
exactly those frames over a steady 440 Hz bed, so both sync and pitch can be measured); tock.mp4 (the same, purple,
120 frames, 330 Hz bed, band and beep on 15-16 and 75-76); face.mp4 (a textured 48 px patch moving 3 px right and
1 px down a frame over flat grey, 90 frames); shaky.mp4 (a detailed still seen through a window shaking up to 24 px,
60 frames, pure shift); music.wav (20 s, 600 Hz); voice.wav (2 s mono); ntsc.mp4 (29.97 fps).

How sure: "certain" = reproduced in the browser and traced to the code; "high" = reproduced, and Premiere's behaviour
is in Adobe's own documentation (cited) or well known; "medium" = reproduced, but Premiere's exact behaviour is from
memory and could differ between versions.

RESULT: 270 checks, 27 failed, the same 27 in two runs (see "RUNS" at the end).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT WORKS (so the failures are read in proportion)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- The trims keep a linked picture and its sound together in nearly every ordinary case: Selection trims, Ripple Edit
  (B) on heads and tails and beside a gap, Rolling Edit (N) both ways, Rate Stretch (R) from the tail and from the head
  (also into a gap), Slip (Y, and it stops at the source's start), Slide (U) between clips and beside a gap (stopping at
  the next clip). In each case the mix's beeps land within a frame (mostly within 3 ms) of the white bands. Alt trims
  one half alone. Linked Selection off trims one half.
- Q and W with V1 and A1 targeted, Ripple Delete of two separate clips, a gap clicked and closed with Delete (refused,
  and said, when sync-locked music or sound lies in the gap), Insert Frame Hold Segment (the sound gets a 2 s gap, the
  rest moves in step, sync-locked music is cut and moved), Speed/Duration at 50% and 200%, with and without Ripple, a
  typed Duration, Reverse (picture and sound reversed in step), and Maintain Audio Pitch (440 Hz stays 440 Hz at 50%
  and 200%, beeps within a frame) all do what they should.
- Transitions: Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Shift+D, Shift+D; a click on a transition chooses it alone; Effect Controls shows Kind,
  Duration, Alignment and the kind's own Direction, Border Width and Border Color, and they take effect (a Wipe From
  Right with an 8 px border measured on the frame); Delete removes only the transition (one History step, Clear
  Transition); the sound transition's kinds; the Effects panel's default durations (0.5 s and 2 s give 15 and 60
  frames); Constant Power keeps the level through a crossfade over handles; a fade to black at the end.
- Masks on Opacity and on effects placed by their numbers (inside and outside measured), Inverted, None; Mosaic over
  the moving patch, Track forward from frame 0 to the end (the mask's keys within 3 px of the patch at frame 60),
  outside untouched, Clear tracking, Esc stopping part way and keeping what was tracked; Gaussian Blur under a
  rectangle mask (soft left, sharp right).
- Warp Stabilizer: Analyze (60 frames, said), Smooth Motion cuts the frame-to-frame shake to under a third, Auto-scale
  leaves no empty edge, Maximum Scale 101% and Stabilize Only show the edges, Method Position with No Motion holds
  every frame within 1.5 px, trimmed afterwards it asks to be analysed again.
- Effect presets: saved with their keyframes and mask, listed first, applied to another clip, kept after a reload,
  deleted for good. Time Remapping: stopwatch and typed keys, the picture slows exactly as the keys say, the sound
  stays at the clip's speed (as the Help says), the stopwatch off restores 100%; a cut through a remapped clip changes
  no frame. Keyframed Amplify follows its keys (-15 dB at 1.5 s, -20 dB after the key).
- Targeting: Overwrite with only V1 targeted, Insert with only A1 (sync-locked V1 pushed with it), drags from the Project
  panel and the Source Monitor (only its In to Out) to V2 (sound to A2) and to A3 (picture to V3), a sound file dropped
  on V1 goes to A1; Color Matte, Bars and Tone (its tone exactly 1 kHz at -20 dBFS), Black Video, a title and rolling
  credits each go on a free or new track, say so, and never cut or move what is there.
- Undo and Redo leave the playhead and all six track header buttons as they are (in the data and as drawn), and the
  buttons are not History steps; locked tracks are left alone by Select All and Delete, clicks and drags; Nest keeps
  picture and sound, double-click opens the nested sequence and the Project panel brings the outer one back.
- Shift+1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7; markers and Ctrl+Shift+M / Shift+M; snapping a dragged clip's head to a marker and its tail
  to the playhead; S; every Edit and Clip menu item with nothing selected or copied says why and changes nothing.
- Export: the box shows only what each format uses (MP4, WebM, MOV, AVI, GIF, WAV, PNG, SRT); the Opus note in the box
  before exporting and in the status line after; MP4 (H.264 + Opus), WebM (VP9 + Opus), MOV (H.264 + PCM), AVI (MJPEG
  + PCM) of an edit with a ripple trim, a frame hold, a dissolve and a title: every frame checked is the right source
  frame, the bands and beeps agree within a frame (within 5 ms for PCM); GIF, WAV (with the hold's silence), PNG of a
  frame in the hold; loudness normalisation to -23 and -14 LUFS reaches the target by ffmpeg's ebur128 (or says what it
  reached) with the true peak under -1 dBTP.
- Project Name, Ctrl+S (the file named after the project), Open project in a new page (same clips, the name kept, the
  offline media said), Link Media brings it back to play; FCP XML back in keeps the clips, the links, the title with its
  words and the Cross Dissolve; EDL back in keeps the clips, the sound and the dissolve.
- The meters move while playing (master and the mixer's A1 and Master) and stay dark for a muted and an empty track;
  View > Safe Margins lights the Safe button and draws the margins; Auto playback resolution is full size for a small
  sequence; drop-frame timecode reads 00;01;00;02 at frame 1800 in the Timeline and the Program Monitor and 00;10;00;00
  typed goes to 17982; no sideways scroll, every menu reachable, trims work, and the Export and Speed/Duration boxes
  fit on a 390 x 844 phone and a 1366 x 768 laptop. No page errors in any section.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
PROBLEMS, MOST SERIOUS FIRST
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
(The quoted text is the check's line in run.py's output.)

1. Q / W with a sync-locked track that has a clip across the edit leave picture and sound out of step (2 s here).
   Checks: "Q with only V1 targeted: the same 60 frames go from sync-locked A1 too, so the clip's sound stays in step
   with its picture (Premiere: ...)" and "Q at 60 with music on sync-locked A3: the same 60 frames are taken out of the
   music too, so it stays in step after the edit (Premiere)".
   Steps: tick then tock on V1/A1 (New project from video files); click A1's target button off; type 60 in the
   Timeline's timecode box; press Q.
   What happens: tick's picture loses its first 60 frames (it now shows its frame 60 at frame 0) and tock's picture
   moves to 120, but tick's sound is not trimmed and tock's sound stays at 180: the whole rest of the sequence is 2 s
   out of step. The status line says "Tracks A1 have clips across the edit, so they were not moved". With music on A3
   (V1 and A1 targeted) Q leaves the music whole, so the music is 2 s out of place against the edit from there on (said).
   Expected: Adobe's page on trimming (helpx.adobe.com/premiere-pro/using/trimming-clips1.chromeless.html) says of
   Ripple Trim Previous/Next Edit to Playhead: "Like the Extract command, a ripple trim to playhead edit does not affect
   clips on other tracks that are locked" or not sync-locked, while unlocked sync-locked tracks have the trimmed region
   removed; so the sound on A1 (and the music on A3) loses the same 60 frames and everything stays in step. The tile's
   own Help also says a linked picture and sound "move, trim and cut together".
   Cause: C.trimTo (VIDEO_CMDS, line 65672) trims only the targeted tracks' clips; for the other sync-locked tracks it
   calls E.rippleShift, which refuses any track with a clip across the edit and only says so. It should clear the same
   frames there (as E.extract does with clearRange on every sync-locked track).
   How sure: certain of what the tile does; high on Premiere (Adobe's own description).

2. Alt-click picks one half of a linked clip, but Delete (and Copy, Cut, Enable, Ripple Delete) then act on both.
   Checks: "Alt-click on the picture, Delete: the picture goes and its sound stays" and "Alt-click on the picture,
   Ctrl+C: one clip is copied (the picture), and the status line says one".
   Steps: Selection tool; hold Alt and click the first clip's picture on V1 (only the picture is selected, as the Help
   says); press Delete (or Ctrl+C).
   What happens: the picture AND its sound are deleted; the sound the person meant to keep is gone. Ctrl+C copies both
   ("Copied 2 clips"). From the code, Ctrl+X, Shift+E (Enable) and Shift+Delete do the same (not run).
   Expected: only the picture goes (Premiere: Alt selects one track of a linked clip, and what is selected is what is
   deleted; Adobe's trimming page describes Alt for one side of a linked clip; the tile's Help: "Alt-click picks one
   alone").
   Cause: selIds() (VIDEO_CMDS, line 65639) adds every selected clip's linked partners whenever Linked Selection is on;
   C.clear, C.copy, C.cut, C.enable and C.rippleDelete use it. The Timeline's own selection (selectClip with alone) is
   right; the partners should come only from the selection itself, which already holds both halves after a plain click.
   How sure: certain.

3. Edit > Duplicate silently overwrites the clip after the one duplicated, and its key Ctrl+Shift+/ does nothing.
   Checks: "Duplicate of the first of two clips that touch: the clip after it is not overwritten (or it says so)" and
   "Ctrl+Shift+/ (Duplicate, as the Edit menu shows it) copies the last clip right after itself, picture and sound".
   Steps: tick then tock on V1/A1; click tick; Edit > Duplicate.
   What happens: the copy of tick (180 frames) is laid over 180-360, so tock (180-300) is wiped out, picture and sound,
   with nothing said (Ctrl+Z brings it back). The playhead also jumps to the end of the copy. Pressing Ctrl+Shift+/ on
   the Timeline does nothing at all (the status line keeps its old text).
   Expected: a duplicate that does not destroy the next clip (inserted, or put on a free track, or at least said);
   Premiere has no Timeline Duplicate (its Ctrl+Shift+/ duplicates a Project item; Alt-drag duplicates a clip where it
   is dropped), so this command is the tile's own and should be safe.
   Cause: C.duplicate (VIDEO_CMDS, line 65836) is Copy, the playhead moved to the selection's end, then Paste, which
   overwrites (E.place). The key: VIDEO_MENUS key() (line 67142) tests e.key === "/" with Shift held, but Shift+/ gives
   e.key "?" on a US keyboard (Playwright gives the same); e.code === "Slash" would work.
   How sure: certain.

4. A ripple trim that leaves a sync-locked track alone no longer says so (the note is wiped).
   Checks: "... the status line says A3 was not moved" (trims) and "with music across the edit on sync-locked A3, Q,
   Ripple Delete, Speed/Duration with Ripple and the Ripple Edit tool each say A3 was not moved" (edits; only the Ripple
   Edit tool fails it).
   Steps: tick and tock on V1/A1, music.wav dragged to A3 at 0; Ripple Edit tool (B); drag tick's tail from 180 to 150.
   What happens: V1 and A1 ripple; the music on A3 is (by the tile's design) left where it is; the status line is empty.
   Q, Ripple Delete and Speed/Duration do say "Tracks A3 have clips across the edit/gap, so they were not moved".
   Expected: the same sentence, as the code means to say it. (Premiere has since 2023 a trim preference, "Ripple trim
   adds edits to keep both sides of trim in sync", that cuts a clip across the edit on another track and trims it with
   the edit; leaving the music and saying so is the tile's choice, and the saying is the least it owes the person.)
   Cause: VIDEO_TIMELINE apply() (line 66214) calls A.status(E.note()) inside the function given to A.exec (line
   66264), which returns nothing; A.exec (VIDEO_APP, line 65485) then sets A.msg to "" because the function returned no
   string. Returning E.note() from that function would keep it.
   How sure: certain.

5. A Selection trim outward stops at a neighbour on one track only: picture and sound then end at different frames.
   Check: "Selection trim outward with the sound blocked 8 frames on by another clip: picture and sound stop at the same
   frame (Premiere)" (and "... and if not, the status line says the sound could not follow").
   Steps: tick's tail trimmed to 150 (a gap to tock at 180); voice.wav opened in the Source Monitor, its first 0.5 s
   dragged to A1 at 158; drag tick's tail on V1 from 150 to 170.
   What happens: the picture ends at 170, its sound at 158 (stopped by the voice clip), nothing said. The two stay in
   step (same start and source in) but no longer end together.
   Expected: both stop at 158. Adobe's trimming page (as in 1): when several tracks are trimmed, the trim stops at
   whichever comes first, and "If the full trim cannot be performed, the amount allowed is used".
   Cause: VIDEO_TIMELINE apply() plain-trim branch (lines 66216-66217): the clip is trimmed first and its partners then
   by what it got, each stopping at its own neighbour. Roll, Rate Stretch, Ripple and Slide already work out the least
   all can move first; the plain trim should too.
   How sure: certain of the tile; high on Premiere.

6. Final Cut Pro XML and EDL lose frame holds, Dip to White and the fades at a clip's free end.
   Checks: "the EDL marks the frame hold as a freeze (an M2 line at speed 0), as editors write one", "EDL back in: the
   frame hold is a still of source frame 60 again", "FCP XML back in: the frame hold is a still again", "FCP XML back
   in: the Dip to White stays a Dip to White", "FCP XML back in: the fade out at the end is kept".
   Steps: the edit in exportsec/project (a 2 s Insert Frame Hold Segment at 60, Dip to White into the clip after it from
   the Effects panel, Ctrl+D at the very end); File > Export EDL and Export Final Cut Pro XML; a new 320 x 240 sequence
   (Ctrl+N); File > Import EDL; File > Import Final Cut Pro XML.
   What happens: the EDL writes the hold as event 003 "00:00:00:00 00:00:00:00 01:00:02:00 01:00:04:00" (no source
   length, the wrong source frame, no M2), and it comes back as 2 s of moving picture from frame 0 (frames 61 and 110
   show source frames 1 and 50, not 60). The FCP XML writes the hold as a clip item with in = out and no speed, and it
   comes back moving too. Dip to White comes back as Dip to Black; the fade out at the end is not written at all (and,
   from the code, nor is a fade in at a clip's head with nothing before it, nor any Wipe, Push or other kind by name:
   each is written as Cross Dissolve).
   Expected: another editor (or Lantern itself) gets the still, the white dip and the fades. CMX 3600 writes a freeze as
   an M2 line with speed 0; FCP 7 XML can carry a speed-0 Time Remap and named transitions with start-black / end-black
   alignment (medium: from memory of what Premiere and FCP write).
   Cause: VIDEO_XCHG srcFrames() (line 65018) uses c.srcIn and srcSpan (0 for a hold) and never c.hold; no M2 is written
   for a hold (speed stays 1); trans() (line 65115) writes only two-sided transitions into a clip and names only Cross
   Dissolve or Dip to Black; readFcpxml (line 65188) reads every other name as Cross Dissolve and only a transition with
   a clip before it.
   How sure: certain of the tile; medium on the exact form other editors write.

7. A transition can be longer than its clips, and one left beside a deleted clip makes the sequence start mid-dissolve.
   Checks: "a dissolve's Duration typed as 300 frames between clips of 180 and 120: it is held to what the clips allow,
   and frame 60 is still the first clip alone (Premiere)" and "Ripple Delete of the clip before a dissolve: the clip
   left starts at 0 at full strength, not half way into a dissolve with nothing (Premiere)".
   Steps: (a) Ctrl+D at the cut, click the dissolve, type 300 in Duration (frames). (b) Ctrl+D at the cut, click the
   first clip, Shift+Delete.
   What happens: (a) the dissolve runs from frame 30 to 330, past the second clip's end, and frame 60 (two seconds
   before the cut) is already 10% the second clip. (b) the second clip moves to 0 keeping its centred two-sided dissolve
   with nothing before it, so frame 0 is about half faded in.
   Expected: Premiere holds a transition's duration to the media and clips it joins; when the clip on one side goes the
   transition goes with it (or becomes one-sided starting at the clip's head) (medium).
   Cause: VIDEO_CONTROLS transPanel's Duration (line 66543) allows 1-600 with no limit from the clips; E.rippleDelete
   and E.remove (VIDEO_EDIT, line 62341) leave the neighbours' tin / tout as they were.
   How sure: certain of the tile; medium on Premiere.

8. Warp Stabilizer's No Motion drifts with its default Method (Position, Scale, Rotation).
   Check: "No Motion with the default Method (Position, Scale, Rotation) on a shake that is only a shift: every frame
   holds still on frame 0 (each within 1.5 px)".
   Steps: shaky.mp4 alone; click it; Effects > Warp Stabilizer; Analyze; Result: No Motion.
   What happens: frames wander up to about 9 px from frame 0 by the clip's end (the raw shake is up to 24 px), measured
   by phase correlation of rendered frames. With Method: Position the same clip holds within 0.1 px.
   Expected: a camera that only shifts is held still whichever Method is chosen.
   Cause (inferred): at frames with the largest moves the least-squares turn-and-scale fit in VIDEO_STAB motion() (line
   65362) is off (one step, between frames 42 and 43, read as scale 0.9955 and a move of 20.70, 15.66 px, where
   Method Position reads 21, 16 and the shake has no scale at all), and path() adds every
   step's error into all later frames. Blocks whose true match lies off the picture may be kept with a wrong in-picture
   match (sad() returns Infinity only for candidate positions off the picture), and 2.5 x the median residual can keep
   several of them.
   How sure: certain of the drift; medium on the cause.

9. Time Remapping sped past the end of the media freezes the last frame for the rest of the clip.
   Check: "sped up past its media, the clip ends where its media does: no frozen last frame shown for the rest of it
   (Premiere)".
   Steps: click tick; Effect Controls > Time Remapping: stopwatch at frame 0, 50 at frame 30, 300 at frame 120.
   What happens: the picture reaches the media's last frame near frame 120 and then shows that frame, still, until the
   clip's end at 180 (two seconds of frozen picture while its sound plays on).
   Expected: in Premiere, speeding part of a clip up with Time Remapping shortens the clip (and slowing lengthens it), so
   no frame is held (medium-high, from memory).
   Cause: VIDEO_RENDER picture() (line 64693) clamps the source time to the media's end; the remap keys never change the
   clip's duration.
   How sure: certain of the tile.

10. After an MP4 export with Opus sound, the status line says "every current player and editor reads it".
   Check: "Export mp4: the note after saving does not claim every editor reads Opus (Premiere Pro does not import Opus)
   (Premiere)".
   What happens: "Saved Sequence 01.mp4 to Downloads. This browser cannot encode AAC sound, so the sound is Opus (every
   current player and editor reads it; an old one may not)". The Export box said before it, rightly, that some
   televisions and older players do not play Opus.
   Expected: no such claim. Adobe's own community manager says of Premiere Pro 25.5 that "the Opus audio track isn't
   currently supported in Premiere" (community.adobe.com/questions-729/pr-25-5-the-rewritten-mkv-support-is-off-1419561);
   Adobe's supported-formats page (helpx.adobe.com/premiere-pro/using/supported-file-formats/supported-file-formats.html)
   lists no Opus. A person who takes the .mp4 into Premiere gets no sound. The .mov choice (PCM)
   is the one to suggest for another editor.
   Cause: VIDEO_EXPORT run(), line 64969.
   How sure: certain of the text; high on Premiere.

11. Keyframes through a speed change: Rate Stretch moves some, Speed/Duration none.
   Checks: "Rate Stretch to half its length: the effect's keyframes move with the clip's own (Opacity's)", "Rate Stretch
   to half its length: the clip's last keyframe is on its last frame, not past its end", "Speed/Duration 200% gives the
   keyframes the same places as Rate Stretch to the same length".
   Steps: Opacity and a Gaussian Blur's Blurriness keyed at the clip's frames 0 and 179; Rate Stretch the tail to 90;
   (Undo) Speed/Duration 200%.
   What happens: Rate Stretch moves Opacity's keys to 0 and 90 (90 is one past the 90-frame clip's last frame) and leaves
   the blur's at 0 and 179, far past the end; Speed/Duration leaves every key where it was. The same speed change by the
   two ways gives two different results, and an effect's ramp is cut off half way.
   Expected: one rule for both ways and for all keys (the clip's own, the effects', the masks'); a key at the last frame
   stays on the last frame.
   Cause: VIDEO_EDIT rateStretch() (line 62493) scales only c.keys, with Math.round (179 x 0.5 = 89.5 -> 90); setSpeed()
   (line 62498) scales none.
   How sure: certain of the tile (what Premiere does with keys on a speed change was not checked).

12. Smaller things
   a. "one Undo takes Shift+D's transitions away, both (one command, one step) (Premiere)": Shift+D is two History
      steps (Apply Video Transition, Apply Audio Transition), so one Ctrl+Z leaves the video dissolve. Cause: VIDEO_MENUS
      line 67157 and the menu item (line 67091) call C.transition twice, each an A.exec. Medium on Premiere.
   b. "... and the Program Monitor's resolution box says 1/2": View > Playback Resolution changes the picture's size but
      the box under the Program Monitor keeps saying Auto. Cause: VIDEO_MONITORS builds the select once (line 65891);
      nothing sets it when A.playRes changes. Certain.
   c. "Ctrl+Z after changing the sound's default duration: the Effects panel's boxes show the durations then in force":
      the two default-duration boxes are History steps (Premiere keeps them in Preferences, out of History) and after
      Ctrl+Z the box still shows 2 s while 1 s is in force. Cause: VIDEO_PANELS durBox (line 66688) is built once.
      Certain.
   d. "the clip stays selected after Esc stops the tracking (its Effect Controls still shown)": Esc stops Track forward
      (as the Help says) but also deselects the clip, so Effect Controls goes blank just when the person wants to see
      the result. Cause: the tracker's own keydown listener (line 66417) and the tile's Escape = Deselect All (line
      67161) both act. Certain; minor.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
OBSERVATIONS (not pass or fail)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Ctrl+D with a clip still selected (from the click before) puts transitions on both ends of the selected clip: at a
  first clip that means a fade-in from black at the sequence's start as well as the dissolve at the cut. The Help's
  example ("put the playhead where the second begins, press Ctrl+D") does not say a selection takes precedence; an
  Adobe forum thread (community.adobe.com/questions-729/selection-follows-playhead-giving-me-transition-issues-in-
  premiere-2024-1411866) suggests Premiere does the same. run.py deselects (Esc) before Ctrl+D so as not to test this.
- The EDL writes a dissolve into a clip with no media before its head as starting at the cut (the tile shows it centred,
  holding the first frame), so it comes back aligned Start at Cut and looks different. A title is written as an event
  named "Graphic" and comes back as an offline clip (said).
- Typing a value in Time Remapping's Speed (%) without the stopwatch changes the picture's speed alone (as Premiere's
  Time Remapping does); a person expecting Speed/Duration gets a picture out of step with its sound. Not checked.
- Warp Stabilizer's analysis and tracked masks (a key per frame) are kept in the project text, in each of the 100 Undo
  copies and in the browser's storage after every change; persist() swallows a full storage silently. A long clip
  analysed could stop the project being kept on the device without a word. Not tested (needs long media).
- On the 390 px phone the Timeline's tracks are 248 px wide beside the 132 px header column; usable, tight.
- Duplicate moves the playhead to the end of the copy (the Help says "wherever the playhead is").

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
NOT TESTED
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- AAC encoding: this Chromium cannot encode AAC, so every MP4 had Opus; the AAC path is untested.
- Premiere itself was not available: "(Premiere)" expectations come from Adobe's documentation where cited, else from
  memory (see "How sure").
- Sound heard through a sound card: headless; the meters were read from their canvases while the Program Monitor played.
- Touch gestures on a phone (the phone layout was driven with a mouse); long media and speed; masks drawn on the
  monitor (the tile places them by numbers only); HEVC, ProRes, 5.1; captions (reviewed before).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
RUNS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Run 1 (python3 run.py, 2 cores, another review's browser running at the same time): 270 checks, 27 failed, 4 min 19 s.
Run 2 (the same, run again afresh): 270 checks, 27 failed, 4 min 17 s. The 270 PASS/FAIL lines are identical in the
two runs, and so is every FAIL line's "what was seen". (An earlier second run was stopped part way from outside;
the one reported here ran to its end.)
Every one of the 27 failures is one of items 1 to 12 above:
  item 1: 2 (Q with only V1 targeted; Q with music on A3)
  item 2: 2 (Alt-click then Delete; Alt-click then Ctrl+C)
  item 3: 2 (Duplicate overwrites; Ctrl+Shift+/)
  item 4: 2 (the A3 note after a Ripple Edit tool trim, in trims and in edits)
  item 5: 2 (the blocked Selection trim, and its "... and if not" line)
  item 6: 5 (EDL M2, EDL hold, FCP XML hold, Dip to White, the fade out)
  item 7: 2 (300-frame dissolve; Ripple Delete beside a dissolve)
